_comment: A stand-in for Commander Spellbook's bulk export and Scryfall's oracle bulk file,
for `node tools/fetch-combos.js out.json --fixture test/fixtures/export.json`.
The field names are the ones their export actually uses, read off a real variant by
`.github/workflows/peek-variant.yml` — run 2290-2919, the default that workflow
carries. THAT WORKFLOW IS WHAT RE-CHECKS THIS FILE. A fixture is a shape somebody
else controls, frozen, so if it ever stops matching, this is the file that is wrong
and not the tool.
Deliberately not a happy path. Every variant below is here for a shape that can go
wrong quietly, and test/fetch-combos-fixture.test.js says which:
101-202      two cards, ids that rebuild exactly
101-303      the same, sharing a card so the intern table has to fold it
202-303      the third pair, which is what solves all three card ids
101-202--7   a template slot, whose id lands in the rebuilt permalink
101-303--9   a requirement with no template id: compact() records null, so the
id cannot be rebuilt and the row must keep the literal one
606-707      two cards that appear nowhere else, so neither id can be solved
and this row keeps its literal id too
Every id here is numeric-dash, because deriveCardIds() reads a row's id AS the
card ids in it. A made-up id like `no-rebuild-1` is not a harmless label: its
parts intersect with the real ones and unsolve every card in the row. The first
draft of this file did exactly that and quietly derived nothing at all, which is
the same class of invisible wrongness the whole fixture is here to catch.
101-404      utility-only results, which fall back to being shown
303-404      a mix, where the utility half is dropped and the rest kept
(last)       no `uses` at all, which compact() drops entirely — so the count
out is one lower than the count in
`lands`, `basicLands` and `mdfc` are Scryfall's half of the fixture, like
`cardIdentity`: names over every card rather than only the ones in combos.
Snow-Covered Island is a land and not a basic, and Bala Ged Recovery is an MDFC —
a spell on the front, a land on the back. Three lists because no one of them
implies the others.
